title: Contributing to ggrank
text: Fork clone repository. Create focused branch. Add update tests documentation implementation. Run devtools::test() devtools::check(). Open pull request describing user problem chosen behavior. package deliberately focuses rankings rank change. New plotting functions reuse common ranking engine answer distinct ranking question rather duplicate established general-purpose chart type. Please never contribute confidential, identifiable, unlicensed data. Teaching datasets must synthetic clearly redistributable compatible licence.

title: Creating your first ggrank plot
text: Users normally supply values rather ranks. Inspect calculation ggrank_data(): Ranking uses exact numeric values. Equal values share competition rank default (1, 2, 3, 3, 5) receive separate alphabetical display positions. categories tied top_n boundary included, top-ten figure can contain ten boxes. filter top N calling package, prevents entrant exit detection. Display formatting independent ranking. example, rank unrounded rate printing prepared one-decimal label:
code: tied_rates <- data.frame(   year = rep(c(2020, 2025), each = 5),   organism = rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"), 2),   rate = c(5, 4, 3, 3, 2, 6, 4, 4, 2, 1) )  ggrank_data(   tied_rates,   category = organism,   period = year,   value = rate ) #>    category period value rank display_position label group #> 1         A   2020     5    1                1     5  <NA> #> 2         B   2020     4    2                2     4  <NA> #> 3         C   2020     3    3                3     3  <NA> #> 4         D   2020     3    3                4     3  <NA> #> 5         E   2020     2    5                5     2  <NA> #> 6         A   2025     6    1                1     6  <NA> #> 7         B   2025     4    2                2     4  <NA> #> 8         C   2025     4    2                3     4  <NA> #> 9         D   2025     2    4                4     2  <NA> #> 10        E   2025     1    5                5     1  <NA> formatted_rates <- transform(   tied_rates,   rate_label = sprintf("%.1f per 100,000", rate) )  ggrank(   formatted_rates,   category = organism,   period = year,   value = rate,   label = rate_label )

title: Build a readable rank-transition table — ggrank_table
text: Produces analytical companion ggrank(). row compares category two adjacent selected states. two-state comparison one row per category; three four states produce successive transition rows 1990 2010 2010 2021.

title: Build a readable rank-transition table — ggrank_table
code: ggrank_table(   data,   category,   period,   value = NULL,   rank = NULL,   label = NULL,   group = NULL,   periods = NULL,   top_n = 10,   direction = c("descending", "ascending"),   ties = c("min", "dense", "first"),   show_transitions = c("boundary", "top_only", "all"),   check_rank = TRUE )

title: Build a readable rank-transition table — ggrank_table
text: data data frame one row per category period. category, period Unquoted columns identifying category ordered state. value Optional unquoted numeric ranking-value column. may omitted authoritative rank column supplied. rank Optional unquoted column containing precomputed ranks. label Optional unquoted display-label column. default value formatted using format(). group Optional unquoted category-group column. periods Optional vector selecting ordering two four states. top_n Rank threshold retain state. categories tied boundary included, result may contain top_n categories. direction Whether large ("descending") small ("ascending") values rank first. ties Ranking method: "min" (default competition ranking), "dense", "first" (unique alphabetical ranks). show_transitions "boundary" retains categories appearing top N selected state; "top_only" includes top-N observations ; "" includes every category. check_rank TRUE, supplied ranks checked disagreements equal values, shared ranks across different values, requested ranking direction. Potential disagreements warn rather fail authoritative ranks may use external tie-breakers additional data.

title: Build a readable rank-transition table — ggrank_table
text: data frame category, transition states, ranks, rank change, values, value change, labels, group, missing-value indicators, movement status. Positive rank_change means category rose ranking.

title: Build a readable rank-transition table — ggrank_table
text: Rank change calculated rank_from - rank_to: positive values rose towards rank one, negative values fell, zero stable. status "entrant" category crosses outside inside top_n, "exit" reverse. boundary statuses take precedence "riser" "faller". "new" "absent" indicate category exists one side; "missing" identifies supplied non-finite value.

title: ggrank 0.1.0
text: Period selections now reject duplicates report selected periods left without finite ranking values using clear, user-facing errors. Missing-value status matching now joins category period safely. ggrank_change() now validates scalar comparisons. Plot layout arguments receive consistent validation, GUI plot downloads available viewing plot. Added synthetic football- cricket-style leaderboard examples, including guidance exporting rankings containing 20 30 rows. Initial implementation ggrank(), ggrank_table(), theme_ggrank(). Support automatic supplied ranks across two four states. Automatic retention categories entering exiting selected top N. Added synthetic causes product teaching datasets. Added ggrank_data() inspecting automatically calculated ranks. Equal values now share competition ranks default; tied categories retain separate display positions ties top-N boundary included. Ranking uses exact numeric values independently printed labels, missing non-finite ranking values produce informative warning. Supplied ranks can now checked value ties ranking direction; potential disagreements warn external ranking rules may valid. Added ggrank_change() visualise largest rises falls ggrank_table() result. Added ggrank_app() optional local Shiny interface existing ranking, table, visualisation workflow. Finalised ggrank_change() latest-comparison diverging chart raw data support, explicit -comparison selection, stable-category control, detailed rank labels, within-comparison ordering, wrapped labels. Added palette, legend-title, legend-label, legend-visibility controls primary visualisations. Added rank-workflows across package GUI. Authoritative ranks can now plotted without inventing value, mark, rate, score column. Reworked GUI four-step guided workflow basic/advanced settings, embedded data examples, independent error handling change chart.
